questions.question: What is a record in Java?
options: An immutable class designed to hold data (Java 16+)
explanations: Correct. A record is a special, immutable class introduced in Java 16 to represent data concisely.
It is not a primitive variable.
It is not a static method.

questions.question: Which methods does a record generate automatically?
options: Constructor, getters (accessor methods), equals, hashCode, and toString
explanations: Correct. A record automatically generates the constructor, accessor methods (one per component), equals(), hashCode(), and toString().
Not only constructor and getters; it generates more methods.

questions.question: How is a record declared?
options: class Persona { String name; int age; }
explanations: Correct. The syntax is record RecordName(type1 field1, type2 field2) {}.
Interfaces are not declared that way and do not have fields.

questions.question: Can additional methods be added to a record?
options: Yes, additional methods can be added
No, a record only has the automatically generated methods
explanations: Correct. A record can have additional methods, static fields, and constants.
It is not limited to static methods only.
It is not limited to private methods only.
